_comment: Hindu expansion 175-drive F: Mahabharata youth, boons and forest exiles (Ganguli 1883-96, public domain).

region.zh: 尼沙陀森林（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Ekalavya episode

summary.en: Rejected by Drona because of his forest birth, the Nishada prince Ekalavya built the master's statue in the woods and taught himself archery before it - becoming better than Arjuna. When Drona came demanding his fee, the boy cut off his own thumb and laid it before him: the epic's most-cited, most-contested parable of caste, loyalty and the price of a guru's word.
summary.zh: 因出身林野而被德羅納拒收的尼沙陀王子以卡拉維亞，在林中立師之像，對像自習射術——技藝勝過阿周那。當德羅納索其學資時，少年自斷拇指奉上：史詩中最常被引用、爭論最烈的關於種姓、忠誠與師言之價的寓言。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition and politically contested (caste readings); classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Drona refused the forest-born boy as a pupil - the teaching was reserved for princes - and Ekalavya went home, made a clay image of the master in the forest, and practiced before it until his hand was as true as the image's face.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: When dogs ran barking through the grove, seven arrows filled their mouths before they could cry; the princes traced the shot to a dark youth with a bow, and Arjuna went to his teacher, wounded in his pride: you promised me the best archer.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Drona came and demanded his fee: thy right thumb. Ekalavya, glad to pay a master he had never been allowed to serve, cut it off at a stroke and held it out; his archery was gone in that instant, and the epic left the cost standing on the page for every age to argue.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Karna's Basket: The Son of the Sun
title.zh: 迦爾納的竹籃：太陽之子

region.zh: 恆河畔，鴦伽王國（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the birth of Karna

summary.en: The maiden Kunti, testing a boon, called the Sun and bore a child already armored: born with golden ear-rings and a breastplate grown into his skin. Afraid, she set the basket on the river; it floated to the charioteer Adhiratha, who raised the boy as his son - and Karna lived his whole life paying for a birth his mother hid.
summary.zh: 少女恭蒂試驗恩賜，召日神而生下一個已然披甲的孩子：生而戴金環，胸鎧與皮肉同長。她因懼而將竹籃置於河上；竹籃漂至御者阿底羅陀之處，他將男孩養作己子——迦爾納的整個人生都在償付母親隱瞞的那次出生。

passages.text: The boon was meant for practice; the Sun came as a bridegroom in full glory, and Kunti, unmarried, bore a child already wearing armor and ear-rings of gold - a birth like a dawn.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The basket was set on the river at dawn; it floated down past reeds and towns to the charioteer's household, where Radha the childless took the armored boy for her own and named him Karna, the ear-ringed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The armor was his glory and his doom: a prince's courtesy could not outface a charioteer's son - and the sun-son's whole career was a bid to be honored as the person the armor proved he was.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Draupadi's Swayamvara and the Fish's Eye
title.zh: 黑公主的自擇婚禮與魚眼

region.en: Panchala, capital of Drupada (symbolic pin at Bareilly)
region.zh: 般遮羅，德魯帕陀都城（象徵性定位於貝拿勒斯以北）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Chaitraratha and Draupadi sections

summary.en: Drupada raised a daughter from fire and a target no one could hit: a fish spinning above oil, to be pierced through the eye with a bow seen only in reflection. Kings failed; a brahmin youth stepped up, strung the bow, and shot the eye - Draupadi's garland fell on a poor student who was five husbands and two gods deep in disguise.
summary.zh: 德魯帕陀自火中生一女，並設下無人能中的的靶：懸於油面旋轉的魚，須以僅能於倒影中看見的弓，貫穿其眼。諸王皆敗；一名婆羅門青年上前張弓，射中魚眼——黑公主的花環落在一個貧寒學生身上，而此人實為五夫二神重重偽裝。

passages.text: The target was a fish eye revolving above a smooth oil-pan, its bow heavy and its line of sight visible only in the oil's mirror - a test engineered so that no mortal aim could take it honestly.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Karna of the golden armor lifted the bow to applause - and was refused by the princess herself, a brahmin-born's match for a suta's son; the slight he never forgave was minted here.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The brahmin youth - Arjuna in beggar's garb - strung the great bow without a glance, took the eye in the oil's reflection, and the hall of kings watched a pauper take the fire-born bride; the brothers' laughter gave the game away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: The Kirata and the Hunter: Arjuna Fights Shiva
title.zh: 基拉多與獵人：阿周那戰濕婆

region.en: Himalayan slopes above the Ganges (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 恆河上游喜馬拉雅坡地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Kiratarjuniya episode), composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Vana Parva, Kirata-Arjuna section

summary.en: To win the weapons that would win the war, Arjuna performed fierce austerities in the Himalayas. When a boar charged him, he and a rough hunter - a Kirata of the hills - shot it at the same instant, and argued over the kill. The argument became a duel, the duel became a wrestling match that Arjuna could not win - and the hunter, laughing, revealed himself: Shiva, holding out the Pasupata, the weapon of destruction.
summary.zh: 為贏得足以贏得戰爭的武器，阿周那在喜馬拉雅行猛利苦行。當一頭野豬衝來，他與一名粗野的山中獵人——基拉多——同時放箭，為獵物之屬而爭。爭論化為決鬥，決鬥化為摔角，而阿周那不能取勝——獵人大笑現身：濕婆，遞出滅盡之器帕沙帕塔。

passages.text: Arjuna's tapas burned so hot that the forest gods came to Shiva in complaint; the god chose the guise least suspected - a Kirata, a hill-hunter with a bow of bamboo and a dog for company.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The boar died with two arrows in it; two hunters claimed the shot. Words went to blows, blows to wrestling - and the archer who felled armies could not move the mountaineer's shoulder.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Exhausted, Arjuna made a clay linga and offered a garland - and the garland was already on the Kirata's neck. The god of gods gave him the Pasupata with the counsel: use it only against a foe no other weapon can end - and the war's arsenal was complete.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Arjuna in Heaven: Indra's Court and the City of Nivatakavacha
title.zh: 阿周那天堂：因陀羅廷與尼婆達迦瓦遮之城

region.en: Svarga, Indra's heaven (symbolic pin at Meru)
region.zh: 須彌山頂因陀羅天界（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Vana Parva, Arjuna's ascent to heaven

summary.en: Indra's charioteer Matali came down and carried Arjuna bodily to heaven, where the god armed him for the war - and sent him first to kill the Nivatakavachas, demons armored in fog that no weapon could touch. Five years of heaven: the Gandharvas taught him music, the apsaras danced, and he returned to earth with every weapon in the gods' inventory.
summary.zh: 因陀羅的御者摩達利下凡，攜阿周那肉身登天；神為戰爭武裝他——並先遣他誅滅披霧之鎧、凡兵莫能觸及的尼婆達迦瓦遮群魔。五年的天堂：乾達婆授其樂，飛天為其舞，他攜諸神武庫之全部歸返大地。

passages.text: Matali's chariot took the sky-road past clouds and stars; in Indra's court Arjuna was welcomed like a returning son - and sent, before any gift, to the city of the Nivatakavachas where the old demons had hidden behind armor of cloud.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The battle was a siege of fog: with the gods' own weapons he cracked the cloud-armor and burned the city, and the heaven's oldest menace was cleared by a mortal's hand.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The five years in Svarga armed the war: the conch Devadatta, the Gandiva bow, horses of the sun's stock, and a curriculum of music and dance - heaven's syllabus for a coming battlefield.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Urvashi's Curse and Arjuna's Eunuch Year
title.zh: 鄔爾伐希的詛咒與阿周那的中性之歲

region.en: Svarga, Indra's heaven (symbolic pin at Meru)
region.zh: 因陀羅天界（象徵性定位於須彌）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Vana Parva, Urvashi and Arjuna

summary.en: In heaven the apsara Urvashi offered herself to Arjuna; he refused with a bow to her years and his father's memory, and her curse fell: he shall live as a eunuch, desired by none. Indra softened the curse to one year of Arjuna's choosing - the year, it turned out, the war would need: as Brihannala the dance-teacher in Virata's court, his eunuch year kept the disguised heroes alive.
summary.zh: 在天界，飛天鄔爾伐希以身相許阿周那；他以其高齡與父親之誼婉拒，詛咒遂落：彼將以閹者之身度日，無人欲之。因陀羅將詛咒軟化為阿周那可自選的一年——而戰爭恰好需要那一年：作為毗羅陀王廷的舞師般厘哈那羅，其閹者之年使偽裝的英雄們得以存活。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition; gender readings contested; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Urvashi came at midnight to the hero's chamber with love written in her walk; Arjuna folded his hands and refused - thou art the wife of my father's prime, and my mother in heaven's eyes.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The apsara's curse answered the compliment's sting: thou shalt wander among women as a eunuch, fit for their music and unfit for their eyes - and Indra, arriving, cut the term to a single year at the cursed one's own choosing.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Arjuna chose the thirteenth year of exile - and the curse became the disguise: in Virata's court as Brihannala, the eunuch dancing-master taught the princess and hid the archer of the age; the war's hinge was a curse, kept.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva and Virata Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

region.zh: 婆羅那婆多（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, the house of lac

summary.en: Dhritarashtra sent his nephews to the festival-town of Varanavata - to a palace built of lac, pitch and straw by Duryodhana's order, ready to burn with them inside. Vidura's warning came in a riddle; the brothers tunneled out under cover of a harmless banquet, set fire themselves, and escaped through the earth while the city mourned their ashes - five bones and a mother, all false.
summary.zh: 持國遣其外甥赴慶典之城婆羅那婆多——入一幢由難敵下令以樹脂、瀝青與茅草所建的宮殿，屋內火起則五人與其母皆焚。維杜羅以謎語警示；兄弟們於無害宴會之掩護下掘地道遁走，自行縱火，於城中哀悼其灰燼之時自地底逃出——五副骨骸與一位母親，盡皆為偽。

passages.text: The palace at Varanavata was handsome and hollow: walls of lacquer, floors of pitch, a bonfire waiting for a festival night - the uncle's love-letter to his nephews, written in kindling.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Vidura's warning arrived in a language the watchers could not read: a house that catches fire from its own walls, said the uncle's riddle - the mouse escapes by digging; the brothers began the tunnel that night.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: On the night of the trap they burned the house themselves and slipped out the tunnel as the lac roared; a Nishada woman and her sons, drugged and drugged into the beds, were burned in their places - and the five Pandavas walked out of the ashes into the epic's next three hundred years.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Bhima and Bakasura, the Village Eater
title.zh: 怖軍與婆迦蘇羅：食村的怪物

texts.period: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Adi Parva, Bakasura episode

summary.en: The rakshasa Bakasura held the village of Ekachakra to a tax of food and flesh, one household's meal and one child a day, carried by a boy on a cart. In disguise as brahmins, the Pandavas drew the turn of the woman of the house - Kunti sent Bhima, who ate the monster's delivery-cart dinner first, then the monster.
summary.zh: 羅剎婆迦蘇羅向一輪村徵收食物與血肉的稅——每日一家之餐與一童，由男孩推車送至。偽裝為婆羅門的般度五子恰好輪到屋主之女送稅——恭蒂遣怖軍前往，他先吃光怪物之車上餐點，再吃掉怪物本身。

passages.text: The tax was simple and terrible: every day a cart of rice, two buffaloes, and a child - carried by the family whose lot had fallen, down the forest road to the cave of Bakasura.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: In the brahmin's rented hut the lot fell to Kunti's household; she sent her second son, the one who ate like ten, with the cart - telling him to enjoy the meal on the way.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: Bhima sat at the cave-mouth and ate the delivery; the monster, insulted, charged - and the wrestle ended when the boy's own arms were used as his last meal. The village's tax died with the eater; the beggars' household was richer by a secret.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Draupadi and Kichaka in Virata's Court
title.zh: 黑公主與毗羅陀王廷的計迦迦

region.en: Virata's city, Matsya (symbolic pin at Jaipur)
region.zh: 毗羅陀王城，摩蹉國（象徵性定位於齋浦爾）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Virata Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Virata Parva, Kichaka episode

summary.en: In the thirteenth year of hiding, Draupadi served as a common maid in Queen Sudeshna's palace - and the general Kichaka wanted her. She refused; he shamed her publicly; she went to Bhima at night, and the general was found at dawn folded into a ball of flesh at the dancing-hall. Her five husbands, all disguised, could do nothing until the corpse spoke: the war's date was set by a maid's ruined honor.
summary.zh: 藏匿的第十三年，黑公主於王后蘇德什那宮中為侍婢——而大將計迦迦欲得之。她拒絕；他公開羞辱她；她夜見怖軍，黎明時大將被發現蜷成一團血肉於舞殿。她的五位丈夫皆在偽裝之中，在屍體說話之前皆無能為力：一名侍婦被毀的名譽定下了戰爭的日期。

passages.text: Kichaka, the queen's brother and the army's pride, saw the new maid at the palace and pressed her with gifts and threats; Draupadi, a maid with five hidden husbands, refused - and he shamed her before the whole court.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: At night she found Bhima at the kitchens, his disguise as the royal cook; they laid the trap at the dancing-hall, and the general who came at midnight was folded like a wet cloth and left where he fell.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The corpse told the story its finder could not: Kichaka's kinsmen tried to burn the maid on his pyre, Bhima rescued her in the night, and the king of Trigarta raised an army to avenge his ally - the heroes' year of silence ended with a war sized to fit.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

title.en: Nahusha, the Serpent King of Heaven

region.zh: 喜馬拉雅，堅戰的林路（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Vana Parva, Nahusha episode

summary.en: When Indra fled heaven after killing Vritra, the gods crowned the mortal Nahusha in his place - and power made him drunk: he rode in a palanquin carried by the seers themselves, touching Agastya's head with his foot. The sage's curse turned him into an enormous python, lying across the forest road until a Yudhishthira came to answer his riddles and free him.
summary.zh: 因陀羅誅弗栗多後逃離天界，諸神立凡人那護沙代之——權力使之醉：他乘由仙人親自抬行的轎輦，以足觸阿竭多之首。仙人的詛咒化他為巨蟒，橫臥林路，直到一位堅戰前來解答其謎而釋放他。

passages.text: Nahusha, a pious king of the lunar line, was lifted to Indra's vacant throne; the court bowed, the apsaras attended - and the seat taught him what thrones teach: that other men are furniture.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: His palanquin was carried by the seers of old; hurrying, he struck Agastya on the crown - and the sage's curse fell like a stone: be the snake you have behaved as, and lie across the world's roads until the right king frees you.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: A python the size of a hill lay on the Pandavas' forest road and seized Bhima; Yudhishthira answered its questions - What is liberation? What is the highest dharma? - and the serpent, satisfied, rose from the dust as Nahusha again, mounted to heaven, and returned Indra's throne unspoiled.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

region.zh: 甘陀摩達那山（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, composition layers c. 400 BCE-400 CE (Ganguli translation, 1883-96)

source.work: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, trans. K. M. Ganguli (1883-96), Vana Parva, Bhima and Hanuman

summary.en: Sent by Draupadi to fetch the scent-lotus of the north, Bhima came to an old monkey lying across the road, who asked the strong man to lift his tail out of the path. The tail would not lift. Enraged, Bhima grew huge - and the old monkey laughed, and grew huger: Hanuman, his half-brother by the same Wind-father, giving his kinsman a lesson in how large the family is.
summary.zh: 受黑公主之遣北上尋取香蓮的怖軍，遇一老猴橫臥路上，請壯士將其尾移出小徑。其尾不可舉。怖軍怒而身漲巨——老猴大笑，身漲更巨：哈奴曼，同以風神為父的異母兄，給其弟上了一課：家族之量。

passages.text: The monkey lying in the mountain road asked only one courtesy: move my tail aside; I am old. Bhima, proud of his strength, pulled - and the tail did not move.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: He tried with shame and then with anger; the monkey, smiling, asked what his strength was for. Bhima grew vast - and the old shape grew vaster, filling the valley: it was Hanuman, son of the same Wind.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.

passages.text: The brothers embraced: Hanuman blessed the quest, promised to ride on Bhima's banner in the coming war, and sent him on to the lotus lake - the Ramayana's hero lending the Mahabharata his tail for a lesson.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Mahabharata, Vana Parva (Ganguli 1883-96); not verbatim.
